# runr_workflow (Resource)

One durable workflow definition declared through the API ([workflows](https://runr.sh/docs/workflows/)): its triggers, retries, timeout, concurrency limits, idempotency key and cancel events. The function's code implements the workflow under this name; the definition says when and how it runs.

The resource declares this one definition (`PUT /api/projects/{project}/workflows/{workflow}`); destroying it archives the workflow (`DELETE …/workflows/{workflow}`). The project's other definitions are not sent and stay as they are, their source too: what the function's SDK reported stays `sdk`. (An API before 0.6.0 has only the set: the resource declares the set again with this definition added, replaced or left out.) Definitions the function's SDK reports (source `sdk`) belong to the code and are refused. `triggers` left out keeps the definition's triggers — for example those of `runr_workflow_trigger`; set, it is the whole list (do not combine both for one workflow). Pausing (`active = false`) survives later declarations and syncs. Runs, events and the signing key are not configuration. Needs `workflows.manage`.

Import with `<project name or id>/<workflow>` or `<project name or id>/<environment>/<workflow>`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# process-order, implemented by the project's code, declared through the API.
resource "runr_workflow" "process_order" {
  project_id  = runr_project.orders.id
  name        = "process-order"
  description = "Charge, reserve stock and ship an order"
  triggers = [
    { event = "order.created", condition = "event.data.total > 0" },
    { queue = "orders" },
  ]
  retries     = 5
  timeout     = "1d"
  concurrency = [{ limit = 1, key = "event.data.customer_id" }]
  idempotency = "event.data.order_id"
  cancel_on   = [{ event = "order.cancelled", expression = "event.data.order_id == async.data.order_id" }]
}

# The nightly report of the staging environment, paused for now.
resource "runr_workflow" "nightly_staging" {
  project_id  = runr_project.orders.id
  environment = "staging"
  name        = "nightly-report"
  triggers    = [{ cron = "0 3 * * *", timezone = "Europe/Istanbul" }]
  active      = false
}

# Triggers left out of runr_workflow can come from runr_workflow_trigger.
resource "runr_workflow" "refunds" {
  project_id = runr_project.orders.id
  name       = "refund"
}

resource "runr_workflow_trigger" "refund_requested" {
  project_id = runr_project.orders.id
  workflow   = runr_workflow.refunds.name
  event      = "refund.requested"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Workflow name, as the function's code knows it (not `app` or `sync`).
- `project_id` (String) Project id.

### Optional

- `active` (Boolean) `false` pauses the workflow: triggers and the API start no runs; runs in progress go on. Left out: a new workflow is active, an existing one keeps its state (e.g. paused with `runr workflows disable`).
- `cancel_on` (Attributes List) Events that cancel matching active runs (at most 10). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--cancel_on))
- `concurrency` (Attributes List) At most two concurrency limits, at most one of them keyed. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--concurrency))
- `description` (String) Description.
- `environment` (String) The project environment whose workflows these are (name or id; [environments](https://runr.sh/docs/workflows/#environments)). Left out: the project's own workload (production).
- `idempotency` (String) Expression of the idempotency key: a second event with the same key starts no run, e.g. `event.data.order_id`.
- `retries` (Number) Retries of a failed step (0–20). Left out: a new workflow gets the installation's default (3), an existing one keeps its value.
- `timeout` (String) Longest a run may take, e.g. `1d` (`500ms`, `30s`, `15m`, `2h`, `1d`, `1w`, combinations, ISO 8601). Left out: no limit of the workflow's own.
- `triggers` (Attributes List) What starts a run: each an `event` (with an optional `condition`), a `cron` schedule (with an optional `timezone`) or a `queue` stream. Left out: the definition keeps the triggers it has (none for a new workflow), e.g. those `runr_workflow_trigger` adds. Set: exactly these (`[]`: none). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--triggers))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) `<project_id>/<name>`, or `<project_id>/<environment>/<name>` for an environment's workflow.

<a id="nestedatt--cancel_on"></a>
### Nested Schema for `cancel_on`

Required:

- `event` (String) Event name, e.g. `order.cancelled`.

Optional:

- `expression` (String) Expression the event must satisfy to cancel a run (`async` is the run's own event), e.g. `event.data.order_id == async.data.order_id`. Left out: every active run.


<a id="nestedatt--concurrency"></a>
### Nested Schema for `concurrency`

Required:

- `limit` (Number) Runs at the same time (1–1000).

Optional:

- `key` (String) Expression the limit counts per value of, e.g. `event.data.customer_id`.


<a id="nestedatt--triggers"></a>
### Nested Schema for `triggers`

Optional:

- `condition` (String) Expression the event must satisfy (`if`), e.g. `event.data.total > 100`; event and queue triggers.
- `cron` (String) Five-field cron expression; one run per due minute.
- `event` (String) Event name, e.g. `order.created`.
- `queue` (String) Redis stream of the project's queue bridge; each message starts a run.
- `timezone` (String) IANA time zone of `cron` (default UTC).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <project name or id>/<workflow> (the project's own workload)
terraform import runr_workflow.process_order orders-api/process-order

# <project name or id>/<environment>/<workflow>
terraform import runr_workflow.nightly_staging orders-api/staging/nightly-report
```
